svg.title: Trusting the installer on a fresh machine: On a network without GitHub, two lines in .env.dist bring the toolbox tools from a mirror
svg.text: Trusting the installer on a fresh machine
Scenario: On a network without GitHub, two lines in .env.dist bring the toolbox tools from a mirror

g.text: Given a machine that cannot reach GitHub, where the six toolbox installers that download
A machine that cannot reach GitHub, in a project with the six toolbox installers that download from it. curl cannot
connect to github.com, and the two GitHub settings of .env.dist are empty, which means GitHub itself.
The developer runs the six installers one after the other. Each one fails, since GitHub is out of reach.

text.tspan: curl -sS https://github.com; grep '^TASK_GITHUB' .env.dist; for t in task betterleaks gum glow jq node; do

g.text: Then once .env.dist names a GitHub mirror, the same six installers all get their tool from
The developer writes the address of the network's GitHub mirror in .env.dist, one for github.com and one for
raw.githubusercontent.com. Here the mirror is the test's own, standing in for the Nexus of a forge.
The same six installers run again, and each one says installed. Every download went through the mirror, and none reached

text.tspan: betterleaks gum glow jq node; do .config/$t/install.sh >/tmp/$t.log 2>&1 && echo "$t installed" || echo "$t
